correctness.rationale: The second-derivative determinant gives -54 times the displayed sextic, a nonzero factor both in characteristic zero and modulo 29. The quartic is geometrically smooth in both: if one coordinate is zero the vanishing gradient equations force all to be zero, while for all coordinates nonzero their product would imply 1=-27. Thus it is geometrically irreducible. At [1:0:0] the two gradients are the y and z coordinate covectors, so the quartic cannot divide the sextic. Independently written and run on 2026-11-24 UTC, reproduce_mod29.py enumerated the 871 disjoint-chart representatives, verified rank two at the 24 common zeros, and found 24 distinct normalized gradients and 276 different cross-products each incident with exactly two lines. The degree-24 Bézout count exhausts the geometric special fiber, not merely its rational points; transversality makes each point simple. The 24 rational points lift uniquely to distinct sections over the henselian DVR by the Jacobian criterion and Hensel, and Bézout in the generic fiber excludes extra points. The ordinary flex property holds in characteristic zero (also established by Elkies; simple Hessian intersections have flex weight one). Tangent gradients have nonzero reduction and reduce compatibly. Equal generic lines would reduce to equal lines; a zero determinant for three distinct generic tangent coefficient vectors would yield a zero determinant at 29. The finite census excludes both. Intersections of distinct transverse projective lines with just two branches are nodes, so the total is 276 and each line meets the other 23 at different points. value.rationale: The 24 inflection tangents of the classical highly symmetric Klein quartic are an intrinsic arrangement. Whether their incidence has special multiple points is a natural question not settled by smoothness, ordinary flexes, a scheme equation in the dual plane, or the incidence behavior of a general quartic. The result gives the complete incidence type needed in arrangement calculations, while cleanly separating these lines from the Klein bitangents and other highly concurrent Klein configurations.
